note: Proposed wording only. The published articles in this preview were not changed.

items.original: Driving with THC in the body above legal limits is an offence in the UK, including with a prescription if you are impaired.
items.proposed: Driving while impaired by a drug is illegal. In England, Scotland and Wales, exceeding a specified drug limit is a separate offence; a statutory medical defence may apply when the medicine was lawfully prescribed or supplied and taken as directed. A prescription does not permit impaired driving. Northern Ireland has a different legal framework.
items.why: The published sentence conflates the specified-limit and impairment offences, omits the conditional medical defence, and uses a UK-wide label without the Northern Ireland distinction.
items.limit: General published-information wording. Not an assessment of any individual driver's legal position. This check does not validate the surrounding cannabis safety or ADHD efficacy sentences.
